bvi_skipper.text: The Sir Francis Drake Channel is a perfect sailing route: steady trade winds, short hops, rum at every stop. It's named for Drake, who sailed it in 1595.
The BVI is 60-odd islands, but only about fifteen are inhabited. The rest are rocks and cays and a lot of seabirds.

then.text: Mind the grotto walls. They've got a few hundred million years on you.

else.text: A clue in the Baths? Go in through the crawl-way. There's a crab down there who guards something. He's very polite about it.
Take your time. The tide comes in. The crab doesn't.
These boulders are granite. They came up from underground and were rounded by weathering. Water shoes, torch, and keep your elbows in.
Some go through the Baths to Devil's Bay. Some turn back. The sensible ones turn back with photographs.

bvi_fisher.text: Fungi's the dish. Cornmeal and okra, stirred hard in a pot and shaped into a dome. We eat it with fish. The band's fungi, the dish is fungi. Everyone else gets confused.
On Anegada they catch lobster by the sackful. Don't ask what I know about it.

then.text: You found it, then. It's behind the rock I was sitting on. Everything always is.
Keep the doubloon. It's not Spanish. It's from the pub. But it's got a good story attached, and so will you.

else.text: I'm looking for treasure. So is Scrope, just over there. He thinks he's first. He is not. Beat him and the dig's yours.
Looking for pirate treasure? Get the clue from the dive shop first. Everyone knows the Rhone, but few know the caves behind Norman Island.
Norman Island: said to have inspired Treasure Island. Pirates hid loot in the caves. I've been here three years and found three crisps.

bvi_home.text: Back to Brize Norton? The RAF's flight leaves from Beef Island, over the bridge, and the pilot waits for nobody. Well, for a wedding, if there is one.
Head home to RAF Brize Norton?

then.text: Right, mind the gap. Mind the other gap too.

else.text: Take your time. We'll be here.
